items.text: Trump left Joint Base Andrews on Monday on Air Force One for Asia, travelling with Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent. His first stop is the ASEAN summit and ASEAN–US special summit in Manila, which runs to Nov 18 and includes a bilateral meeting with President Marcos. Trump said the visit would be mostly about economics and promised a major speech. From Manila he goes to APEC in Shenzhen, and he said he might meet Kim Jong Un during the China leg; the Daily Tribune calls that uncertain.
items.notes: The Tribune says the trilateral was not formally confirmed as of Nov 17. That conflicts with E-261116-01, where all three governments confirmed it. The Kim meeting is Trump's own speculation. Local protests are planned near the summit venue (Tribune sidebar). Could not read the NPR article (blocked).

items.text: The Financial Times reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is considering a return and has discussed it with confidants. Silicon Valley allies are lobbying the board, setting up a 'war room' of tech executives and seeking White House support. A 'Bring Jensen Back' open letter is backed by Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney and signed by some Nvidia employees. Investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker urged the board to keep all options open. Treasury Secretary Bessent, by contrast, called on Sunday for a 'dramatic shake-up' of Nvidia's leadership. The FT also says the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor, while the board says no formal search has begun. Nvidia and Huang declined to comment.
items.outlet: Financial Times (via The Irish Times); CNBC
items.notes: Based on the FT's sources. The Haas approach is unconfirmed. The board's independent probe into Huang's conduct is ongoing.

items.text: US stocks were mostly lower on Monday ahead of Nvidia's earnings and the Anthropic IPO. Yahoo Finance's live page showed the Nasdaq down about 0.9%, the S&P 500 down about 0.4%, the Dow roughly flat (+0.1%) and Nvidia down about 2.3%; CNN described a slide to start a major week. Brent crude held around $92–96 a barrel after renewed Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain offset a well-supplied physical market.
items.notes: The index figures come from the live page's ticker and may not be official closing levels; the AP closing table could not be read. Sources give conflicting Brent figures ($92 vs about $96).

items.text: Saturday's unofficial Alaska Division of Elections count has Mary Peltola at 140,637 first-choice votes (49.94%) to Sen. Dan Sullivan's 129,424 (45.96%), leaving her 157 votes short of an outright majority. AP estimates 97% counted and has not called the race. Overseas ballots can arrive until Nov 18. If no one passes 50%, ranked-choice tabulation starts Nov 18, with certification targeted for Nov 25. Sullivan has not conceded and his campaign wants a complete count, while Peltola's campaign says he has no path. DOJ is appealing the Nov 1 dismissal of its suit to block certification.
items.outlet: Newsweek; Anchorage Daily News; The Hill
items.notes: Figures are unofficial. Newsweek's own ranked-choice model has Peltola at 51.8%, which is not official. Democracy Docket (left) frames Trump's 'voter confusion' claim about the two Sullivans as collapsing. Could not read the ADN article (blocked).

items.text: NBC News reports that PAHO is expected to announce officially on Tuesday (Nov 17) that the US has lost measles-elimination status. Until then, the reports rest on sources familiar with a commission vote. HHS said the CDC has mounted an aggressive response, including $100 million in extra funding in October, and that Secretary Kennedy and CDC Director Erica Schwartz still recommend the MMR vaccine. Schwartz said losing a designation does not mean abandoning an evidence-based approach. NBC notes the CDC has held no media briefings or vaccination campaigns this year. Cases top 5,400, the most since 1991. States report 10 deaths, at least four of them babies too young to be vaccinated.
items.notes: No PAHO statement had been published as of this writing.

items.text: Flights were close to normal on Monday after the Nov 13 ground stop. At 6:30 a.m. ET FlightAware showed about 250 cancellations and 850 delays, against more than 2,300 cancellations on Sunday. CBS, citing senior government sources, reports the fault was limited to Cisco 600-series routers made in 2001–2006. The FAA has not decided whether human error or a faulty router was to blame. FAA chief Bedford said instability spread to 17 facilities and there is zero evidence of foul play, and DHS Secretary Mullin said there are no signs of a cyberattack. Reps. Larsen and Carson said FAA and DOT staff would brief the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee on Monday on the administration's extra air-traffic-control funding request.
items.notes: CBS puts the extra funding request at $30 billion, while earlier reports cited Duffy's $50 billion; the figures conflict. Fast Company reports the FAA had been warned about risks in its telecom upgrade (headline only; not read).

items.text: US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV in Boston issued a final ruling striking down the DHS rule that capped international students' and scholars' stays at four years. The rule would have replaced the open-ended 'duration of status' policy for F, J and I visa holders. Saylor found it arbitrary, capricious and not in accordance with law. He had blocked it temporarily on Sept 14, a day before it was due to take effect, and the government's appeal of that order is pending. France 24 reports the ruling also covers limits on foreign journalists' visas.
items.notes: The DHS response and whether the vacatur applies nationwide were not stated in the sources read. An appeal is likely.

items.text: The US military rejected the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, saying US forces intercepted two Iranian attack drones, and the US Embassy urged Americans to stay vigilant. The NYT and Axios report the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group has joined two other carriers in the region. Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said a path to ending the war is open if Washington accepts Iran's conditions, and the foreign ministry ruled out curbs on enrichment. Iranian state TV claimed tankers using an unauthorised Hormuz route had hit mines, with six vessels burning since Sunday.
items.notes: Accounts of US interceptions differ: Military.com says two drones were downed Sunday, while Rigzone has CENTCOM downing two on Friday. The tanker-mine claim comes from Iranian state media; UKMTO separately reported one tanker attacked in the Gulf. Neither is independently confirmed.

items.text: With four legislative weeks left before Democrats take over, Democrats say they will back a spending bill before the Dec 11 deadline only if it cuts off defense money for the Iran war, and Senate Majority Leader Thune called that complicated. Sen. Patty Murray floated a continuing resolution, which Republicans are reluctant to take up. Trump wants a $350 billion defense supplemental in a final party-line reconciliation bill, which some Republicans resist. Senate Republicans also plan to keep members in town to confirm judges.
items.notes: Deseret is centre-right. The Democratic condition is as reported there and was not cross-checked with a left-leaning outlet.

items.text: On Monday the head of the President's Chancellery, Zbigniew Bogucki, chaired talks at the Belweder on resolving the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) crisis. PiS, Konfederacja, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej, Rozwój Plus, Razem, PSL and Polska 2050 attended; KO, the Left and the Centrum group stayed away, and President Nawrocki and PM Tusk did not attend. Bogucki called the talks difficult but a success: participants agreed to start work on constitutional changes now, the Chancellery is to present a combined proposal on Tuesday, and the next meeting is set for Wednesday 18 Nov at 17:00. He acknowledged that none of the groups whose votes are needed to amend the constitution took part. Presidential spokesman Rafał Leśkiewicz attacked the absent parties, and Bogucki dismissed Tusk's own proposals as PR.
items.notes: KO argues the TK needs no political 'reset' because it already works normally, and Tusk says repair is under way. Rzeczpospolita's headline stresses that the plan proceeds without KO and the Left, while TVN24 foregrounds the Palace's attacks on the absent parties. Rzeczpospolita has Bogucki presenting the combined proposal at Wednesday's meeting, while TVN24 says it will come on Tuesday afternoon or evening. A right-wing outlet (wPolityce) could not be read; only a TV Republika headline quoting Bogucki that Tusk wants unlimited power was seen.

items.text: At the Belweder talks, PSL presented the most far-reaching proposal, a constitutional amendment, according to Bogucki. The National Assembly (Sejm and Senate jointly), acting on a KRS motion, could declare by at least 336 votes that the Tribunal is permanently unable to function. It would then elect all 15 judges at once, for staggered 3-, 6- and 9-year terms, from candidates put forward by the Sejm Marshal after consulting the heads of the Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court, with the President's prior consent. A Sejm public hearing on the proposal is planned for Thursday.
items.notes: A constitutional amendment needs a two-thirds Sejm majority. Without KO and the Left it cannot pass.

items.text: On the eve of the Nov 17 TK General Assembly, convened by Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska to rule on lifting Bogdan Święczkowski's immunity and allowing his detention, his lawyer Bartosz Lewandowski sent letters dated Friday 13 Nov to the police chiefs, the National Prosecutor's Office, ABW, SKW and CBA. The letters warn that detaining Święczkowski without consent from a 'lawfully constituted' assembly would be a crime. He argues that judges sworn in at the Sejm rather than before the President have no judicial status and that the assemblies of 3 and 10 Nov were invalid, and he cites the Supreme Court's 10 Nov ruling lifting Święczkowski's suspension. Korwin-Piotrowska maintains that this Supreme Court ruling has no effect and that eight judges make a quorum.
items.notes: The lawyer's claims come from a pro-PiS outlet. Prawo.pl notes that constitutional scholar Ryszard Piotrowski and the Helsinki Foundation question the legal basis of the suspension itself. The assembly had not yet taken place when this was written (about 06:30 on Nov 17).

items.text: The Digital Affairs Ministry announced the end of the main phase of restoring public e-services after the foreign cyberattack. The most-used services are back, mostly via e-Doręczenia: residence registration, civil-status extracts, PESEL checks, child passport applications and ID-card status checks. The state IT centre COI said only four ePUAP services are working again, including a general letter to an office, notice of a vehicle sale or purchase, and requests for public information. Work on full restoration continues, and no attacking country has been named.
items.notes: The status comes from official statements carried by a regional portal; gov.pl pages could not be fetched.

items.text: NBP data show core inflation excluding food and energy fell to 2.9% year on year in October from 3.1% in September, with no change month on month. Inflation excluding administered prices fell to 3.5% from 4.1%, excluding the most volatile prices to 3.3% from 4.0%, and the 15% trimmed mean held at 2.8%. Headline CPI was 3.5%, down from 4.1%.

The Standing Committee of the Council of Ministers took up the Energy Ministry's bill to freeze household gas prices for 2027 on Monday, and the full government is due to consider it on Tuesday 17 Nov. The bill caps the price at 197.29 zł/MWh net, the 2026 tariff level, for households, housing cooperatives and communities, schools, hospitals, care homes, churches and shelters, with no declarations needed for households. Sellers would be compensated from a fund financed by a 10% levy on the net revenues of large gas importers; the government puts the cost at about 6.2bn zł. URE-approved tariffs would remain for protected customers until end-2030. The ministry estimates the cap saves households between 77 and 1,863 zł a year.
items.notes: The Standing Committee's decision itself was not found. A Rzeczpospolita analysis, cited in a digest, suggests Orlen would bear much of the levy.

items.text: President Nawrocki hosted Estonia's new president, Ülle Madise, in Warsaw. He said the shared priority is strengthening NATO's eastern flank and protecting Baltic critical infrastructure, and described Russia's threat as hybrid as well as military. Madise said Poland fully understands Estonia's decision to close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December. She welcomed Poland's invitation to the December G20 summit in Miami, calling Poland a spokesman for the region.

Arriving at the EU Foreign Affairs Council in Brussels, Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said losing its most lucrative hydrocarbon market is the heaviest sanction on Russia: it sells less oil at prices at least 30% lower, which limits its ability to fund the war. He criticised the planned Trump–Putin–Xi meeting on Nov 19 on the margins of APEC as needlessly elevating Russia to superpower status, and said the format should be China, the US and the EU.
items.notes: These are opinions attributed to Sikorski. Outcomes of the Council meeting were not checked.

items.text: The Sejm Health Committee will consider the Senate's eight amendments to the anti-alcohol law on Wednesday, 18 Nov. The amendments would lift the ad ban for 0% beer (adopted by a single vote), allow sales in airport and free-zone areas despite the night ban, and allow producers to sponsor sports events. They would also exempt craft-beer events from the promotion ban, move the start date to 1 June 2027 and give shops until 2030 to remove logos from fridges. Health Ministry representative Kuba Sękowski said the amendments are exceptionally harmful to public health.
items.notes: The date of the plenary vote was not given.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała sent the City Council his first draft budget, for 2027. It plans revenue of 10.93bn zł, spending of 11.88bn zł and a deficit of about 956.9m zł. The city says that is about 319.5m zł less than this year's deficit, while the operating surplus rises to about 389m zł from roughly 51m zł. New borrowing would be about 927m zł and debt repayments 212.7m zł. The city claims about 300m zł in savings, mainly from promotion, tourism and administration, and says it is protecting education (a record 4.21bn zł) and transport (about 2.43bn zł, including a return to cheaper fares and 339m zł for stage IV of the KST tram). The multi-year forecast aims for a surplus in 2029.
items.reporter: Michał Banach; Anna Winiarska; Grzegorz Bąk
items.outlet: Puls Krakowa; TVN24; Krakowski Raport; Kurier Krakowski
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: Krakowski Raport reads it differently. Spending still rises by 412m zł (+3.6%), the smaller deficit comes mostly from Finance Ministry forecasts of higher PIT (+419m zł) and CIT, and only 75m zł of the claimed 300m zł in savings is itemised. It also points to cuts the city's announcement leaves out: culture -53.7m zł, sport -37.2m zł. Gibała posted on X that the deficit falls by 350m zł; official documents say 319.5m zł. Kurier Krakowski stresses that debt keeps growing, and TVN24 quotes the deputy mayor calling Kraków's debt the worst of Poland's big cities. No opposition councillors are quoted in any of the coverage found. First reading is due at a session by 2 Dec; the 18 Nov agenda does not include it (BIP).

items.text: According to KRKnews, Gibała sent a letter to city officials and the boards of municipal companies demanding strict spending discipline. Each expense is to be judged by what it gives residents. Promotion, marketing, events and catering are to be cut back to what is necessary, while education, public transport and social assistance are protected. The article reports no specific savings amounts and no timeline.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor

items.text: Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister coordinating the special services, told Rzeczpospolita that the 24-year-old behind the 7 Nov Main Square attack was interested in mass murders and their perpetrators. Siemoniak said there are no grounds so far to see an ideological motive, and no outside influence has been identified. He said the attack was planned, not impulsive, citing evidence and the attacker's online activity. Separately, prosecutor Eryk Stasielak told PAP that investigators have established the attacker's route but are still looking for CCTV footage; the motive remains under investigation.
items.notes: These are the minister's statements; prosecutors have not yet published formal findings on motive or on accomplices. Krakowski Raport adds that the prime minister has ordered recommendations for changing the law on storing weapons at home.

items.text: Gibała set out three ways to commemorate the six people killed on 7 Nov: leave the bullet marks in place, put up plaques, or commission an artwork such as a mural or installation. He says residents and councillors will decide, by the end of January 2027. He also said that if no relatives claim the attacker's body once prosecutors are finished, the city will ask Jagiellonian University's Collegium Medicum to take it for medical and scientific use. Otherwise the municipality must pay for the burial. A UJ spokesman told Super Express that no request has arrived and the university will not speculate.
items.outlet: Kraków Portal; RMF FM; Wirtualna Polska; Super Express
items.notes: No decision has been made on the body. WP reports that relatives buried three victims in Waśniów on 16 Nov.

items.text: Gibała says the Christmas market on the Main Square and late-November and December events will go ahead in their usual form; the city has asked the police commander whether extra security is needed. The temporary concrete barriers on streets leading to the Main and Small squares stay for now. The city has money for modern retractable bollards on all approach streets, to be installed next year with co-funding promised by the voivode. The government has still not answered his request for 10m zł for the security and monitoring centre; without it, he says, the opening slips from 2027 to 2028.
items.notes: This is a roundup of the mayor's statements; we found no separate official text on the bollards.

items.text: Slovak President Peter Pellegrini presented Medals of Gratitude in Bratislava to two young Slovaks, Linda Trnková and Mario Mačina. They were in Kraków on a day trip during the 7 Nov attack and left shelter to resuscitate a badly wounded woman and dress her wounds. Pellegrini passed on thanks from Polish President Karol Nawrocki.
items.notes: RMF spells the names as Trnkova and Maczina.

items.text: Deputy PM and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz attended the foundation-act ceremony for the new headquarters of the Military Medical Forces Command (Dowództwo Wojsk Medycznych, created in 2025). The site is the 6th Command Battalion grounds on ul. Ułanów. The four-storey building for about 250 people is being built by the Military Property Agency and is due for handover by 29 May 2028; the minister suggested it could be ready in early 2028. He said Kraków has become a real centre for the army's development. No cost was given.

MP Daria Gosek-Popiołek says she will ask the Supreme Audit Office (NIK) to examine the city's 2018 no-tender sale of a riverside plot at ul. Kościuszki 38/Jaskółcza 3 to the AZS AKF club at a 90% discount, for about 111,000 zł. Developer K38 CORE PROJEKT now plans a water-sports centre there with about 110 rooms (92 of them hotel rooms), a restaurant and a spa. The city issued the demolition and building permit on 2 Sep; residents have appealed. The 10-year window for recovering the discount is approaching.
items.notes: The article includes no response from the city or the developer.

items.text: GDDKiA is repairing a damaged expansion joint on the A4 Kraków bypass viaduct over the railway between the Skawina and Południe junctions, on the carriageway towards Katowice. From 16 Nov the work occupies the hard shoulder, with an 80 km/h limit. From Wednesday 18 Nov to Friday evening 20 Nov the road narrows to one lane over 600 m, around the clock.

The city opened public consultations on how much it will pay in 2027 to non-public nurseries and children's clubs for each child. Comments are accepted until 11 Dec. On 18 Nov the council will also take a residents' draft resolution on nursery grants (druk 1492), which the mayor opposes.

The city-owned Narutowicz Hospital says it has raised about 24m zł in outside money since July 2025, including an 11.2m zł digitisation project, a leased surgical robot and new equipment. KRKnews points out that the hospital lost 26.5m zł in 2025 and had more than 65m zł in overdue liabilities at the end of 2025, despite city support under a 45m zł recovery programme.

Researchers at the Kraków University of Technology (Politechnika Krakowska), led in the article by Dr Przemysław Zaręba, are developing molecules that block serotonin receptors on cancer cells. The work started with glioblastoma and now covers drug-resistant prostate and breast cancer; prostate work is in in-vivo preclinical studies. They say clinical trials could take 3–5 years if funded.

The city says it has no grounds for now to expect a lasting fall in tourism after the 7 Nov attack, though it accepts short-term changes in bookings are possible. It points to long-running visitor surveys and to safety rankings (Riviera Travel, InsureMyTrip), but gives no post-attack booking or cancellation data.

Commerce Ministry data released on Nov 16 put wholesale (WPI) inflation for October at 12.29%, up from 11.39% in September and the highest in the 2022-23 base series. Fuel and power inflation rose to 32.84% from 25.85%. Primary articles rose to 9.24%, while food (8.58%) and manufactured products (9.54%) eased slightly. The all-commodities index was 113.3. It is the third straight monthly rise and follows October CPI of 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling.
items.notes: Official Commerce Ministry release via multiple outlets. Ind-Ra had projected above 12%. It is not stated whether September's figure was revised.

items.text: IMD said the Bay of Bengal deep depression strengthened into Cyclonic Storm Akvan on the evening of Nov 16, moving north-northwest at about 8–10 km/h. IMD expects a severe cyclonic storm by Nov 18 and a very severe cyclonic storm around Nov 19. It is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Nov 20, with winds of 120–130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h. Heavy rain is forecast for Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and parts of south Bengal, and fishermen have been told to stay ashore.
items.notes: The Hans India piece is internally inconsistent: it gives both Machilipatnam on Nov 19 and Nellore–Tuni on Nov 20. The Nellore–Tuni/Nov 20 window matches India.com and The Watchers. The IMD bulletin itself was not fetched.

items.text: The Congress-led INDIA bloc asked the Supreme Court for permission to put 48 written questions to CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the two Election Commissioners and the ECI's Director General (IT). Congress said the questions include how often the ECs disagreed with the CEC, who decided to hold the nationwide SIR, and who ordered changes to Form 6 and the centralisation of ERONET/ECINET. Congress says the ECI's affidavit did not address its 'vote theft' allegations. The batch of pleas against the CEC and the SIR is listed before the CJI Surya Kant bench on Nov 17.
items.outlet: DT Next (IANS); Daily Pioneer; National Herald
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Content of the questions is per Congress. No ECI response to the 48 questions was found. The ECI disputes the underlying allegations in its affidavit. No Swarajya coverage of this specific filing was found. The Congress-aligned National Herald frames it as accountability; the ECI has said its processes are lawful.

items.text: A Supreme Court bench of Justices MM Sundresh and P.B. Varadi suspended the life sentences of Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Modhiya, two of the 11 men convicted in the 2002 Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murders case, and granted them bail pending their appeals against a 2017 Bombay High Court ruling. The court cited more than 17 years in custody and arguable issues of fact and law. It noted that one appellant has a severe disability and another was not named in the FIR. The order is dated Oct 28 and was reported on Nov 16.
items.outlet: The Week; ANI; The News Minute
items.notes: The order is dated Oct 28 but only became public on Nov 16. No Gujarat government or victim reaction was found.

items.text: According to a government statement carried by PTI, online self-enumeration for Phase II (population enumeration) of Census 2027 opened on Nov 16 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand, all states going to the polls in 2027, and runs until Nov 30. House-to-house enumeration there runs from Dec 1 to Jan 4, with a reference date of Jan 5, 2027. In other states and UTs, self-enumeration runs Jan 10–24 and house-to-house counting Jan 25–Feb 28, with a reference date of Mar 1, 2027. Manipur's process is on hold.
items.notes: The articles do not say whether caste questions are included. Self-enumeration portal: se.census.gov.in.

items.text: A five-day US FAA assessment of the DGCA's safety oversight began on Nov 16 and runs until Nov 20. It covers aircraft operations, airworthiness and personnel licensing under the International Aviation Safety Assessment programme. India currently holds Category 1. A downgrade to Category 2, as happened in 2014, would bar Indian airlines from adding US routes. Ahead of the visit, the DGCA ran audits that it says found serious findings at four major airlines.
items.notes: The dates are widely reported in advance. No official confirmation that the visit began was found. Results are not expected immediately.

items.text: The Sensex rose 510 points (0.63%) to 82,102.85 and the Nifty 146.8 points to 25,291.10 on Nov 16, led by FMCG and banks, although declining shares outnumbered advancing ones by about two to one and mid- and small-caps fell. HDFC Sky reports foreign investors have bought a net $8.9 billion of Indian equities so far in November, a record monthly inflow, as global AI-stock worries push funds toward India. Brent eased to about $95.40 as Hormuz shipments recovered. Tata Motors PV fell 8.7% after cutting JLR's margin guidance.
items.notes: The record FII-inflow claim is from a brokerage report and was not checked against NSDL data.

items.text: UP Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, at a BJP 'chintan baithak' in Mathura ahead of the 2027 assembly election, said that after Ayodhya it is now Mathura's turn, a reference to the Krishna Janmabhoomi dispute, and taunted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. The two-day meeting, ending Nov 17, brings together national president Nitin Nabin, BL Santhosh and CM Yogi Adityanath. Separately, SP–Congress seat-sharing talks for UP begin on Nov 17, with Congress reportedly claiming about 181 seats. Congress has formed screening committees for five 2027 poll states, with Ajay Maken heading UP's.
items.notes: Maurya's remark is a political claim. The Krishna Janmabhoomi–Shahi Idgah dispute is before the courts. The 181-seat figure is a Congress claim reported by Amar Ujala. No reaction from Scroll or Swarajya was found.

items.text: Six people were killed when a bus fell about 100 m from a bridge into a gorge in the Gular area of Tehri Garhwal, Uttarakhand, early on Nov 17. Initial reports said 30–35 people were aboard, and SDRF teams rescued about 20 injured. CM Pushkar Singh Dhami ordered treatment for the injured and help for victims' families.
items.notes: Toll from early live-blog reports; may change.

items.text: Delhi's average AQI rose back to 246 ('poor') on the morning of Nov 17, from 218 a day earlier, and is forecast to slip toward 'very poor' as winds weaken. Outlook reports GRAP curbs remain in force. The MCD said it issued over 15,400 challans and collected about ₹1.62 crore in pollution fines from Nov 2 to 16.
items.outlet: Business Standard; Business Today; K News India
items.notes: Outlook's headline says GRAP Stage III continues; other reports describe Stages I–II. GRAP stage not confirmed with CAQM.

items.text: The ICC Board, meeting in Bali, confirmed India's Jay Shah, who was unopposed, for a second term as ICC chair. A roundup reports the board also set India to host the 2029 Champions Trophy (Oct 9–28) and to co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup with Bangladesh. Also on Nov 16, Sonia Gandhi launched her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in Delhi.
items.notes: The tournament hosting details come from the AffairsCloud roundup and were not checked against the ICC release.
